title: Cross-SDK stateful tool session patterns and examples (TS/Python/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers want consistent developer ergonomics across TypeScript/Python/Go when using long-lived model sessions that call external tools, emit structured outputs, and support resumable/streaming delivery. Current SDKs have subtle differences in iterator semantics, envelope framing, and error propagation which lead to cross-team confusion and fragile integrations.

Goal: Deliver a set of cross-language patterns, compact interface examples, and reference implementations that demonstrate: 1) stateful session lifecycle for tool-enabled invocations, 2) streaming structured output (typed JSON chunks) with partial validation, 3) a compatibility shim that accepts legacy framed events and normalizes them to the new envelope, and 4) clear migration guidance and tests.

Scope: Produce example snippets and a canonical design that can be included in SDK docs and shipped as example packages for TS/Python/Go. Do not modify runtimes or API servers in this ticket; this is an SDK/design deliverable.

Out-of-scope: full port of all client languages, automated codemods, or changes to server-side event format (will be coordinated separately).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical interface documented for TypeScript: async iterator + .callTool(context, toolSpec) pattern
Canonical interface documented for Python: async generator + session.call_tool(context, tool_spec) pattern
Canonical interface documented for Go: channel-based stream + Session.CallTool(ctx, spec) examples
Compatibility shim implemented in each example that normalizes legacy framed events to the new envelope format
Integration test harness that replays recorded server-side event traces and asserts structural typing and error propagation for all three SDK examples
Code samples published to the SDK repo under examples/stateful-tool-sessions and linked from the Console docs
Migration playbook and checklist added to Confluence with example PRs and rollout notes
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting — aligned on goals and scoped to examples + docs. Decided to keep server contract fixed and implement normalization client-side.
2026-03-03: Prototype TS iterator pattern completed. Found edge case where partial JSON tokens arrive across frames; added buffered-JSON reassembly helper.
2026-03-06: Python async generator prototype completed. Chose to expose a small SessionContext object to hold tool metadata and KV cache handles.
2026-03-09: Go design review — agreed on channel-of-events approach and helper that yields typed events via a decoder goroutine. Noted additional CI flakiness around race on cancellation.
2026-03-11: Compatibility shim spec added — supports legacy envelope v1 and new envelope v2; maps tool-invocation states and error codes consistently.
2026-03-12: Began integration test runner using recorded event fixtures; initial run passes core happy-path for TS and PY, Go requires fix for closed-channel handling (assigned).
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer client-side normalization to avoid server-side breaking changes and to allow gradual rollout to clients that opt into the new envelope.
Framing decision: use newline-delimited JSON envelopes (ndjson) for streaming with a small preamble field 'event_type' and 'sequence_id' to enable idempotent replays.
Ergonomics: expose minimal SessionContext across SDKs that provides .callTool, .emitEvent, and .checkpoint() to support resumability without leaking runtime internals.
Error model: unify transient (retryable) vs terminal tool errors; propagate structured error objects with codes (e.g., TOOL_TIMEOUT, TOOL_BAD_RESPONSE).
Performance note: buffered-JSON reassembly adds <5% CPU in microbenchmarks; acceptable vs developer ergonomics improvements.
Backward compatibility: shim will accept legacy 'frame_type' fields and translate to 'event_type' with deterministic mapping.
test_plan: Unit tests: per-language helpers (buffered reassembly, decoder) with edge cases for split JSON tokens and invalid payloads.
Integration tests: replay 50 recorded server traces (happy path, tool timeout, partial tool output, reconnect) and assert structural conformance.
E2E smoke: run example apps in CI that spin up a local mock server and exercise tool invocation flows with streaming structured output.
Performance: benchmark memory and CPU on example long-lived session (100k tokens, 50 tool calls) and record baseline for SDK-2026.03 release notes.
Observability: add a per-example trace link to Console dashboard so we can surface latency and error breakdown for SDK example traffic.
